key_insight: Fe or Cr substitution at Ni grain-boundary planes increases cohesion, with gains depending on element type and local atomic structure.
engineering_relevance: Atomistically predicted grain-boundary cohesion can inform continuum fracture models for multicomponent Ni-based alloys.
method: Compute DFT rigid-body separation curves for six symmetric-tilt Ni grain boundaries.
Extract work of separation and maximum traction using the universal binding energy relation.
Validate ML interatomic potentials against DFT, then sample finer alloy concentrations and ternary Ni56Fe20Cr24 configurations.
evidence_signal: One tested ML foundation potential quantitatively reproduces DFT work of separation and maximum traction, enabling broader configuration sampling.
watch_item: Binary alloying trends do not quantitatively capture Fe–Cr interplay; explicit ternary calculations remain necessary.
paper_title: Alloying effects on the interface cohesion of grain boundaries in the Ni--Fe--Cr system
